Definition: Ammiel, the name of three or four Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Ammiel belongs to three men, and the Bible keeps them apart by their sons. Ammiel the son of Gemalli is the spy from Dan who goes up to search the land; Ammiel of Lo-debar is the father of Machir, in whose house Mephibosheth is hidden until David sends for him; and Ammiel is the father of Bathsheba, called Eliam in Samuel, whose daughter becomes the mother of Solomon.
TheologicalSignificance: Three households, one name: one Ammiel sends a spy, one shelters a cripple, and one gives a daughter to the king.
